title: Stability Runway and On-call Embargo Protocol for Staggered Launches
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: When we run staggered launch waves across runtime/console/API surfaces, we observe an operational pattern where on-call teams receive concentrated bursts of incidents near cutover windows. This leads to noisy telemetry, delayed rollbacks, and inconsistent rollback criteria across teams.

Goal: Define a cross-team 'stability runway' and formalize a temporary on-call embargo policy and launch window constraints that reduce incident noise and give engineers deterministic signal windows to evaluate model/runtime regressions. The policy should be lightweight (do not block launches) and support canary->wave rollouts with clear escalation triggers.

Scope: Runtime, Console, API launches that touch model-serving behavior, kernel changes, batching/config defaults, or routing policies. Not in scope: major infra capacity purchases, long-lived architectural rewrites.

Deliverables:
- Stability runway definition and duration matrix by launch type (canary, phased, full)
- On-call embargo checklist and minimal contact roster during critical windows
- Runbook additions: telemetry slices, signal thresholds, and rollback escalation flow
- Launch window contract template (owner signoff, blackout times, opt-out criteria)
- Dashboard view in Console for runway state and active embargo windows

Success metrics (first 3 months):
- 30% reduction in post-cutover P1/P2 paging within 2 hours of wave start
- >90% adherence to launch window checklist for tracked launches
- Faster decision time for rollback (median decision latency reduced by 25%)

Acceptance criteria:
- Product + Eng + SRE reviewed and approved the runway matrix document (Confluence link in comments)
- On-call embargo checklist appended to Launch Conductor template and visible in the launch calendar UI
- A pilot run across one runtime canary and one console feature with postmortem documenting signal fidelity
- Dashboard tile showing active embargo windows and owner contacts in Console-ops workspace

Trade-offs and constraints:
- Narrower embargo windows reduce noise but may mask slow-onset regressions; we will use staged signal tiers to mitigate this.
- Additional coordination increases planner overhead; we propose a templated 'auto-accept' for low-risk patches to avoid friction.

Open questions:
- What SLO deltas are acceptable during the runway before a rollback is mandatory? (SRE input required)
- Can Dedicated customers opt out of embargo windows for their private deployments? (legal/compliance check)
- How should model-quality flakiness (nondeterministic model outputs) be surfaced differently than infrastructure regressions?
